STAGE 1 of a 4-stage pipeline on /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui.

YOUR JOB: independently VALIDATE OR DISPROVE four claims about styling placement and test coverage, by EXECUTION where possible. You are the proof stage — a later agent implements only what you confirm. Do NOT fix. Do NOT commit. Read-only except temporary probes you delete (end with a clean `git status`).

Allowed: `npx vitest run`, `npx tsx -e` (importing the real theme is very useful here), `npx tsc --noEmit`, `node`, git reads, Playwright via node_modules/playwright-core against the RUNNING dev server at http://localhost:3000 (read-only page loads).
FORBIDDEN: `npm start`, `npm run build-storybook`, `npx test-storybook` — another process owns those and a concurrent build collides.

Read `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` first — it is the authority, and its "hierarchy" section (5 rungs) is what claims S8/S9/S10 are measured against.

=== CLAIM S5 ===
`overrides/app/hooks/useSubscribeModal.ts` — its **Tab focus trap** (the FOCUSABLE query, the `disabled` filter, the forward last→first wrap and the shift first→last wrap) and its **body-scroll lock** (`document.body.style.overflow` save/restore) have ZERO test coverage anywhere. Claim: ~16 lines, the most intricate logic in the file, and it becomes production-critical the moment `enableNameCapture` flips to true.
PROVE by: exhaustively searching every `*.stories.tsx` and `*.test.*` in the repo for anything exercising those paths — `{Tab}`, `shift`, `tab()`, `overflow`, `body.style`. Use case-insensitive greps; a case-sensitive miss is not absence. Then state precisely which lines of the hook ARE covered and by what, and which are not. Assess whether a Storybook `play` can even express a Tab-trap assertion (does `userEvent.tab()` respect a trap implemented via a document-level keydown listener with preventDefault?) — if it cannot, say so, because that changes what the fix should be.

=== CLAIM S8 ===
`overrides/app/theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` — its `error` part (~line 169) sets fontFamily + fontSize + fontWeight + lineHeight + fontStyle individually, and this is a 1:1 reimplementation of the registered `textStyle: 'body2'`. Same for the `input` part (~line 122) minus lineHeight. Claim: rung 1 of the hierarchy says use `textStyle` for anything textual, never a raw fontSize; the sibling file `footer.ts:158` already writes `textStyle: 'body2'` for the same face; `zimmTextInput.ts` uses `textStyle` zero times while `footer.ts` uses it nine times.
PROVE by: importing the real theme, printing `textStyles.body2`, and comparing value-by-value against what those recipe parts resolve to (the recipe uses `var(--zimm-*)` — resolve those against `zimmTokens.ts` to compare numerically). Report whether it is EXACTLY equivalent or differs on any property. CRITICAL: if you propose replacing with `textStyle: 'body2'`, first check whether anything in those parts depends on a property `textStyle` would not set, and whether a `textStyle` inside a multipart recipe part actually resolves (test it) — if `textStyle` does not work in that position, the claim's fix is invalid even if the duplication is real.

=== CLAIM S9 ===
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmLogo/index.tsx:32-39` puts `display/width/maxWidth/height/overflow` in a raw DOM `style={{}}`, bypassing the theme system — no token resolution, no responsive props. Claim: it is the only new atom with no theme recipe, it has a `variant` prop (exactly the "varies by variant" case rung 3 exists for), and `chakra.svg` was available. The `...style` spread at :38 is legitimate prop forwarding; the base object is not. The `useToken` call at :23 is separately justified because an SVG `fill` attribute needs a concrete value.
PROVE by: reading the file, confirming what is in the style object vs forwarded, and verifying the `useToken` justification is real (does an SVG `fill` attribute accept a CSS var? test it). Then assess feasibility: would moving these to a recipe actually work given the component renders an inline `<svg>` with a viewBox and a hardcoded max-width? Measure the rendered logo against the dev server to establish the current baseline any fix must preserve (it renders in the footer).

=== CLAIM S10 ===
`overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx` composes styles at the call site in three places:
  ~458-462  __css={{...styles.columnHeading, ...(showContactChannels ? {paddingLeft:'2xs'} : {})}}
  ~475-480  identical spread on styles.linkListItem
  ~497      sx={label.includes(NBSP) ? {width:'min-content'} : undefined}
Claim: values are fine but placement is wrong — the style VALUES live in the render tree where rung 3 (the recipe) should own them; the correct shape is `__css={cond ? styles.partA : styles.partB}` and a ZimmNavItem variant/prop for the min-content case. Claim: the `paddingLeft: '2xs'` conditional is duplicated verbatim twice, violating DRY.
PROVE by: confirming the three sites and the duplication. Then — most important — establish whether the proposed fix is VIABLE: for the `sx` case, does `ZimmNavItem` currently accept a variant or prop that could carry `width: min-content`, and would adding one require changing its public API (which matters, since it is consumed by the footer in several places)? For the two spreads, would adding two new recipe parts to `ZimmFooter` be straightforward, and does the part count/parts-array need updating (verify parts/baseStyle parity at RUNTIME, not by regex — a static regex on footer.ts gives a wrong answer). Measure the current rendered paddingLeft on the contact column heading and the link list items so a later agent has a baseline to preserve.

FOR EACH: **CONFIRMED** / **DISPROVED** / **PARTIALLY CONFIRMED**, commands and output as evidence, and — if confirmed — the minimal fix PLUS an explicit viability verdict (is the proposed fix actually implementable without changing a public API or breaking rendering?). Distinguish execution-proof from reasoning. A disproved claim, or a confirmed-but-not-worth-fixing verdict, is a valuable result.

End with `git status --porcelain` proving the tree is clean.

## CLAIM S5 — **CONFIRMED** (with one correction, and the fix-shape question answered)

**Zero coverage — proven by exhaustive absence.** Case-insensitive greps across every `*.stories.tsx`, `*.test.ts(x)`, `*.spec.*` and `*.feature` in the repo for `tab`, `shift`, `overflow`, `body`, `focus`, `trap`, `scroll`, `keydown`, `preventDefault`:

- `overflow` → **0 hits repo-wide in any test artefact.** The scroll lock is untouched.
- `trap`, `scroll`, `keydown`, `preventDefault` → **0 hits.**
- The only tab-ish hits are `userEvent.tab()` in `zimmNavItem/index.stories.tsx:110` (unrelated component) and prose comments in `footer/index.stories.tsx`.
- No `useSubscribeModal.test.ts` exists (`overrides/app/hooks/` has tests only for `useContentfulClient`, `useCountryConfig`, `useZimmTextInputState`).
- No E2E touches it — `e2e/` contains exactly one feature/spec pair (`SMOKE-homepage-load`).

**What IS covered**, and by what — `overrides/app/components/footer/index.stories.tsx` `SubscribeModalOpen` (+ `SubscribeSubmit`):
| Hook lines | Covered? | By |
|---|---|---|
| 40–42 mount effect | implicit | dialog renders at all |
| 45–52 open branch (`triggerRef`, `setTimeout`, first-input focus) | **yes, asserted** | `expect(firstName).toHaveFocus()` |
| 55–58 focus restore | **yes, asserted** | `expect(trigger).toHaveFocus()` |
| 75–77 Escape branch | **yes, asserted** | `userEvent.keyboard('{Escape}')` |
| 99–103 listener add | implicit (Escape works) | — |
| **63–70 body-scroll lock** | **NO** | nothing |
| **79–94 Tab trap** (guard, FOCUSABLE query, `disabled` filter, first/last, both wraps) | **NO** | nothing |

**Line-count correction:** the Tab trap alone is lines 79–94 = 16 lines; the scroll lock is 63–70 = 8 more. The claim's "~16 lines" undercounts the combined total (24) — it is exact for the Tab trap only.

**Can a Storybook `play` express a Tab-trap assertion? YES — proven by execution, and mutation-tested.** I wrote a throwaway Vitest probe (deleted) that mounts the *real* `useSubscribeModal` and drives it with `userEvent.tab()` / `userEvent.tab({shift:true})`. All 3 assertions passed (forward wrap, shift wrap, scroll-lock save/restore). A separate mutation-control probe with identical markup and **no trap** confirmed the assertions genuinely detect the trap: unwrapped forward Tab lands on `<body>`, unwrapped Shift+Tab lands on the outside `open` button — neither is the wrapped target.

Source-level confirmation of *why* (`@testing-library/user-event` `dist/cjs/event/dispatchEvent.js`, identical in the root 14.4.3 and Storybook's bundled 14.6.1):
```js
wrapEvent.wrapEvent(()=>target.dispatchEvent(event));
if (!defaultPrevented) { behaviorImplementation(); }   // <- its own Tab focus move
```
